title: 100kg and Above: How to Start Exercising at Home
intro: You can start exercising at home right now, with no jumping and no equipment. Start with short sessions, low impact moves, and support from a chair or wall.
muscles: Whole body: legs, glutes, chest, arms and core. It also slowly trains your heart and stamina.
steps: March on the spot while holding the back of a chair for 1 minute. Lift your knees only as high as is comfortable.
Sit down and stand up from a sturdy chair 5-8 times. Use your hands to help if needed.
Wall push-up: hands on the wall at shoulder height, slowly bend your elbows towards the wall, push back. Do 8 times.
Stand holding a chair, slowly lift one leg out to the side, lower it. Do 8 times each leg.
Slowly rise onto your toes while holding a chair, lower your heels. Do 10 times.
Rest 1 minute, repeat. Finish with slow walking around the house for 2-3 minutes.
mistakes: Starting too hard, for example jumping straight into jumping workout videos. This can put pressure on your knees and make you give up quickly.
Feeling that only long sessions are worth it. Consistent 5-10 minute sessions mean more than one long session that leaves you sore for a week.
Relying only on exercise to lose weight. Fat loss comes from a combination of portion-aware eating and daily movement.
easier: Do all the moves seated on a chair (seated marching, leg straightening, forward punches). Or start with just 5 minutes of walking.
harder: Add a 3rd round, or add 10-20 minutes of walking on other days. Once you are stronger, use a slightly lower chair for sit-to-stand, without using your hands.
dose: 1-2 rounds (about 5-10 minutes), 3-4 times a week for the first 2 weeks. After that, add a little at a time based on comfort.
safety: Stop immediately if you have chest pain, dizziness, unusual shortness of breath or sharp joint pain. If you have high blood pressure, diabetes, heart problems or recently had surgery, see a doctor first before starting.

faq.q: I get out of breath quickly. Is that normal?
faq.a: Breathing a bit faster during exercise is normal. Simple test: you should still be able to say a few words. If you can't talk at all, slow down or rest.

faq.q: Should I walk or do home workouts?
faq.a: Both are good. Many of our clients start with a mix: light home workouts 2-3 times a week and walking on other days, for example after dinner.

faq.q: Do I need to stop eating rice?
faq.a: No need. Rice can fit into your plan. Try reducing your portion slightly, and add vegetables and protein like chicken, fish or eggs to your plate.
